title: my server is a phone now
excerpt: rooting a CMF Phone 1 to run my personal infrastructure at home.
content_html:
For a while, my personal infrastructure lived on a small Hetzner VPS. It ran a few web apps, a remote browser called Surf, Caddy, and the usual supporting cast. Nothing particularly serious. It worked, I just didn’t like paying for it.

One of the apps I run, Surf, made the compromise difficult to ignore. The cheapest shared machines were fine until Chrome had real work to do, at which point they felt starved. Dedicated CPU machines fix that, but cost enough each month to make a personal browser feel like a questionable financial commitment.

Buying another machine wasn’t an appealing escape hatch either. DRAM prices have gone completely stupid, so putting together a new box with a comfortable amount of memory felt especially ill timed. I looked at used mini PCs and briefly considered turning my desktop into a server whenever I wasn’t using it. Then I remembered the CMF Phone 1 I already own.

Eight ARM cores, 8 GB of RAM, 128 GB of flash, Wi-Fi 6, a 5G modem, and a built in battery backup, that is all attached to an SoC that I feel is overqualified for sitting in a drawer. And I had already paid for it. After dusting it off and playing with it for a while, I decided to turn the phone into the server.

Today it runs Surf and its managed Chrome instance, my personal finance tracker, a screen sharing service, and a handful of smaller web apps. They survive reboots, deploy from Git, and remain reachable when the phone moves between networks, so this is now the machine that actually replaced the VPS.

the first bad idea: replacing android

The cleanest version of this idea seemed to be flashing a normal Linux distribution. The CMF Phone 1 has a postmarketOS device port, it boots, and the device page has enough green boxes to make a reckless person optimistic. I ended up being that person.

What I paid less attention to was everything marked broken: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, hardware acceleration, and most of the other things that make the phone useful as a small server. I got as far as the postmarketOS splash screen and a black display. At that point I had neither a server nor a phone.

Recovering stock Nothing OS turned into its own side quest. The flashing utility needed Windows, so I installed Windows in QEMU, fought USB passthrough and MediaTek drivers, watched the flashing tool hang, then eventually moved the process to an actual Windows installation and restored the factory images.

There was a moment in the middle of this where the phone was soft bircked and only showed a black screen and I genuinely thought I had converted a perfectly good device into a paperweight.

It came back, and lesson learned: Android already has working drivers for every piece of this hardware. Wi-Fi, power management, the battery, the GPU, the modem, and every weird vendor detail already work. Throwing all of that away in pursuit of a more conventional userspace was the wrong trade.

I didn’t actually need the phone to become a normal Linux machine. I needed it to run Linux applications reliably while Android continued doing the hardware specific work it is good at.

termux is the host operating system

The second attempt kept stock Android and treated Termux as the host environment.

Termux gives me OpenSSH, runit, Caddy, Cloudflared, package management, and normal enough Unix tooling. Termux:Boot starts the supervisor and SSH after a reboot. Tailscale gives the phone a stable private address, so from any machine on my tailnet I can just run:

ssh cmf

Termux is not a virtual machine. Its processes still execute against Android’s Linux kernel, but its Bionic based userspace is different enough from an ordinary Debian installation that existing Linux application images cannot simply be dropped into it. That split ended up being useful, though: Termux could remain the small host control plane while each application brought the Linux filesystem it expected.

The actual services are supervised by runit. Android’s battery management is very good at its normal job and very bad for a device pretending to be a server, so I had my Ansible build also apply an Android host profile: it installs a persistent wake lock, disables light and deep idle, exempts Termux, Termux:Boot, and Tailscale from background restrictions, disables the child process limiter, prevents Wi-Fi suspension, and configures Tailscale as the always on VPN.

The recovery chain matters more than any individual setting. Android boots, always on VPN brings Tailscale back, Termux:Boot starts runit, runit starts every resident service, and health checks verify the local and public paths. The phone can reboot without waiting for me to notice.

Android boot
  -> Tailscale always-on VPN
  -> Termux:Boot
  -> runit
  -> resident services
  -> local and public health checks

This isn’t a conventional Linux server. There is no systemd, no normal Docker daemon, and no reason to pretend otherwise. But it is a Linux kernel with a very capable userland sitting on top of it, and that turns out to be enough.

the second bad idea: proot

Most of my applications already shipped as Linux ARM64 OCI images. proot-distro made those surprisingly easy to run under Debian without changing the applications themselves.

PRoot intercepts filesystem and process operations in userspace and makes a regular Termux process believe it lives inside a Debian root filesystem. It isn’t a container boundary. Everything still shares Android’s kernel, network namespace, and Termux UID. But as an application compatibility layer, it is extremely useful because it needs neither root nor a special kernel.

The ordinary web services initially ran fine this way. Each of my applications got a verified root filesystem, a loopback port, and a runit service. Caddy ran directly in Termux and routed hostnames to those ports.

The performance/latency sensitive Surf browser workload was the exception. Starting processes, opening libraries, walking paths, reading browser profiles, and shuffling capture data all crossed PRoot’s userspace translation layer. There was CPU available, but Chrome could not reach it efficiently. So I rooted the phone, not to replace Android, but to mount the same Debian filesystem properly and enter it with a real chroot.

Runit still owned the lifecycle from Termux, configuration still came from the same place, and application data still lived in Termux storage. The workload simply reached Android’s kernel through native syscalls instead of PRoot. The improvement was not subtle!

Once that path was solid, leaving the smaller residents under PRoot stopped making much sense. They now run the same way. My workstation resolves each ARM64 image to an exact digest and exports its filesystem; Ansible verifies and installs it on the phone. A small root helper creates a private mount namespace, binds the required paths, enters the filesystem with chroot, drops privileges, and starts the original image entrypoint.

Neither Docker nor a compiler needs to exist on the phone. These are still compatibility environments rather than security boundaries: the residents share Android’s kernel and network stack, while the private mount namespaces mainly keep mounts and cleanup predictable.

I also spent far too long trying to bridge Debian’s graphics stack to the phone’s Mali GPU through VirGL and Android Vulkan. I got hardware compositing checkmarks alongside corrupt pages and worse performance… The boring software rendered path turned out to perform better.

infrastructure! not a pile of shell history

By this point the phone could run everything, but I didn’t want a pet server assembled from commands I would forget in a week. I moved the entire host into an Ansible managed state: versions, service definitions, routes, power settings, secrets, and health checks all live in one private repository.

The deployment flow is roughly:

release or OCI image
  -> checksum/digest pinned in Git
  -> Ansible over SSH
  -> versioned files on the phone
  -> atomic current symlink
  -> runit service
  -> local health check
  -> public edge check

Releases are pinned by digest or checksum and installed into versioned directories behind an atomic current symlink. A failed checksum or health check stops the deployment, rollback means reverting the pin and applying again. Application data lives separately from releases.

After the small manual bootstrap: install the three Android apps, root the phone, grant Termux superuser access, and authorize SSH, the same repository owns the rest. From my workstation, bringing the host to the declared state is deliberately simple:

make phone
make phone-status
make phone-edge-check

Applying it again does not replace unchanged runtime files or restart healthy residents. More importantly, the configuration is useful if this phone dies: another rootable ARM64 phone can be brought toward the same state without reconstructing a shell history.

Secrets are not stored on the phone’s Git checkout, because there is no Git checkout. Ansible Vault values live encrypted in the infrastructure repository. The vault password is derived by asking my 1Password SSH agent to sign a fixed challenge, so the private key stays in 1Password and the phone never needs access to it. During deployment, Ansible renders only the runtime values each service needs into Termux’s private storage.

getting traffic to a phone behind home internet

The next problem to tackle was ingress. My home connection does not come with the kind of static server setup a VPS gives you, and I don’t want to expose SSH or a collection of random application ports through the router. I also wanted the phone to remain a phone in one important sense: I should be able to unplug it, take it somewhere else, connect it to the internet, and still have my server.

The HTTP applications use a Cloudflare Tunnel. Cloudflared makes one outbound connection from the phone, Cloudflare sends each hostname through it, and Caddy routes the request to the correct loopback service.

Internet
  -> Cloudflare Tunnel
  -> Caddy on 127.0.0.1
  -> application on 127.0.0.1

There is no inbound router rule for those services. Cloudflared only needs an outbound connection, so if I move the phone to another network, the tunnel reconnects and the hostnames follow it. Tailscale does the same for administration. The phone’s battery can bridge the move, and the public services do not care which Wi-Fi happens to be underneath them.

The Surf remote browser backend needed a different path though. Its direct connection is latency sensitive, terminates its own TLS, and the old iPad that connects to it pins the server identity. At home, Cloudflare DDNS keeps a DNS only record pointed at the current public address and the router forwards one port to Surf. On the LAN, the iPad connects directly to the phone.

That still left roaming. A normal Cloudflare Tunnel terminates TLS at Cloudflare, which is exactly what Surf’s pinned connection does not want. The solution was to wrap the complete Surf TLS stream inside an ordinary WebSocket. Cloudflare sees and forwards the WebSocket, but the actual authenticated Surf connection remains encrypted end to end inside it.

This obviously adds latency, from outside home I usually see roughly another network round trip, and the iPad connection was around 60 ms when I first tested it. But it works through a tunnel that only needs outbound connectivity, on an operating system from 2012, without installing Tailscale on the iPad.

That was the moment the phone setup became slightly ridiculous in the best way. I left it plugged in at home, went to the office, SSHed from my MacBook through Tailscale into my workstation and the phone, and used the original iPad through the phone hosted Surf instance. The VPS was no longer, it felt liberating.

what is actually running

The machine has two layers. Android and Termux own the hardware, networking, ingress, and supervision. The Linux residents get the filesystem they expect and otherwise stay out of the host’s way.

layerresponsibilitypieces
Android / Termux hosthardware, networking, ingress, supervisionrunit, Tailscale, Caddy, Cloudflared, DDNS, operations dashboard
rooted Linux residentsapplication compatibility and workloadsSurf and Chrome, Finances, Screen Share, some other apps

The demanding workload is Surf, which brings a modern Chromium browser to old iPhones and iPads. The phone runs desktop Chrome (recent arm64 release of Chrome) and the Surf backend inside its Debian runtime, an iPad mini receives H.264 video and audio while sending touch, keyboard, tab, and navigation commands back. Surf is why I cared so much about syscall overhead and latency in the first place.

Alongside it, the phone hosts my personal finance tracker. It records recurring income and expenses, one time transactions, monthly spending limits, and projects my balance forward day by day. Unlike the replaceable application artifacts, its SQLite database contains state I care about, so it has automated off device backups and a tested restore path.

None of those names are baked into some grand “phone server framework.” A new resident is another immutable artifact, a runit definition, an explicit data contract, a health check, and optionally a Caddy route.

The latest addition is observability. I can still SSH in, inspect runit, tail logs, check public routes, and query Android directly, but I no longer have to do that merely to see what’s going on with the machine at a glance: One native service collects CPU usage for all eight cores, memory, storage, uptime, battery, thermals, local and public reachability, and every discovered runit resident. It keeps bounded history and serves an embedded Vue interface at https://dash.cmf, reachable only over the LAN or tailnet.

The log view discovers the same service directories at runtime, so adding another resident doesn’t require teaching the UI its name. It is much nicer than SSHing in just to remember which thing was noisy.

should you do this?

If you already have a reasonably modern, rootable ARM64 phone sitting unused, this is much less ridiculous than it sounds. You get quiet hardware, low power consumption, flash storage, Wi-Fi, a built in display for recovery, and a battery that behaves like a tiny UPS. Stock Android already supports the hardware, while Termux and a rooted chroot are enough to run a surprising amount of normal Linux software.

I would not put irreplaceable data on one without automated off device backups, and I would not treat the chroots as hostile workload isolation. Rooting expands the trust boundary, Android remains an unusual server host, and software rendered desktop Chrome is not going to beat a dedicated workstation with a GPU.

But for a handful of personal services, especially when the alternative is paying indefinitely for a VPS that is either slow or annoyingly expensive, it is a genuinely useful option rather than only a stunt.

The phone is still a weird server. It shares one kernel, Android occasionally needs to be reminded not to “optimize” it, and a future Android update could always create a new surprise.

But it is quiet, battery backed, fast enough, reachable from anywhere, reproducible from Git, and already sitting in my house. I started this trying to save money on a VPS. I ended up with a rooted phone running my personal infrastructure, and somehow that is much more satisfying. :)

blocks.html_en: Today it runs Surf and its managed Chrome instance, my personal finance tracker, a screen sharing service, and a handful of smaller web apps. They survive reboots, deploy from Git, and remain reachable when the phone moves between networks, so this is now the machine that actually replaced the VPS.

sentences.en: Today it runs Surf and its managed Chrome instance, my personal finance tracker, a screen sharing service, and a handful of smaller web apps.
sentences.zh: 如今，它运行 Surf 及其托管 Chrome 实例、我的个人财务跟踪器、屏幕共享服务以及一些较小的网络应用程序。

sentences.en: They survive reboots, deploy from Git, and remain reachable when the phone moves between networks, so this is now the machine that actually replaced the VPS.
sentences.zh: 它们可以在重新启动后存活下来，从 Git 进行部署，并且当手机在网络之间移动时仍然可以访问，因此现在这台机器实际上取代了 VPS。

blocks.html_en: the first bad idea: replacing android

sentences.en: the first bad idea: replacing android
sentences.zh: 第一个坏主意：替换android

blocks.html_en: The cleanest version of this idea seemed to be flashing a normal Linux distribution. The CMF Phone 1 has a postmarketOS device port, it boots, and the device page has enough green boxes to make a reckless person optimistic. I ended up being that person.

sentences.en: The cleanest version of this idea seemed to be flashing a normal Linux distribution.
sentences.zh: 这个想法最干净的版本似乎是刷新一个普通的 Linux 发行版。

sentences.en: The CMF Phone 1 has a postmarketOS device port, it boots, and the device page has enough green boxes to make a reckless person optimistic.
sentences.zh: CMF Phone 1 有一个 postmarketOS 设备端口，它会启动，并且设备页面上有足够的绿色框，足以让鲁莽的人乐观起来。

sentences.en: I ended up being that person.
sentences.zh: 我最终成为了那个人。

blocks.html_en: What I paid less attention to was everything marked broken: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, hardware acceleration, and most of the other things that make the phone useful as a small server. I got as far as the postmarketOS splash screen and a black display. At that point I had neither a server nor a phone.

sentences.en: What I paid less attention to was everything marked broken: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, hardware acceleration, and most of the other things that make the phone useful as a small server.
sentences.zh: 我不太关注的是所有被标记为损坏的东西：Wi-Fi、蓝牙、硬件加速以及大多数其他使手机用作小型服务器的东西。

sentences.en: I got as far as the postmarketOS splash screen and a black display.
sentences.zh: 我得到了 postmarketOS 启动画面和黑色显示屏。

sentences.en: At that point I had neither a server nor a phone.
sentences.zh: 那时我既没有服务器也没有电话。

blocks.html_en: Recovering stock Nothing OS turned into its own side quest. The flashing utility needed Windows, so I installed Windows in QEMU, fought USB passthrough and MediaTek drivers, watched the flashing tool hang, then eventually moved the process to an actual Windows installation and restored the factory images.

sentences.en: Recovering stock Nothing OS turned into its own side quest.
sentences.zh: 恢复Nothing OS库存变成了它自己的支线任务。

sentences.en: The flashing utility needed Windows, so I installed Windows in QEMU, fought USB passthrough and MediaTek drivers, watched the flashing tool hang, then eventually moved the process to an actual Windows installation and restored the factory images.
sentences.zh: 刷机实用程序需要 Windows，因此我在 QEMU 中安装了 Windows，与 USB 直通和 MediaTek 驱动程序进行了斗争，看着刷机工具挂起，然后最终将该过程转移到实际的 Windows 安装中并恢复了出厂映像。

blocks.html_en: There was a moment in the middle of this where the phone was soft bircked and only showed a black screen and I genuinely thought I had converted a perfectly good device into a paperweight.

sentences.en: There was a moment in the middle of this where the phone was soft bircked and only showed a black screen and I genuinely thought I had converted a perfectly good device into a paperweight.
sentences.zh: 中间有一瞬间，手机软了，只显示黑屏，我真的以为我已经把一个完美的设备变成了镇纸。

blocks.html_en: It came back, and lesson learned: Android already has working drivers for every piece of this hardware. Wi-Fi, power management, the battery, the GPU, the modem, and every weird vendor detail already work. Throwing all of that away in pursuit of a more conventional userspace was the wrong trade.

sentences.en: It came back, and lesson learned: Android already has working drivers for every piece of this hardware.
sentences.zh: 它回来了，并吸取了教训：Android 已经为该硬件的每个部分提供了可用的驱动程序。

sentences.en: Wi-Fi, power management, the battery, the GPU, the modem, and every weird vendor detail already work.
sentences.zh: Wi-Fi、电源管理、电池、GPU、调制解调器以及每一个奇怪的供应商细节都已经可以工作了。

sentences.en: Throwing all of that away in pursuit of a more conventional userspace was the wrong trade.
sentences.zh: 为了追求更传统的用户空间而抛弃所有这些是错误的做法。

blocks.html_en: I didn’t actually need the phone to become a normal Linux machine. I needed it to run Linux applications reliably while Android continued doing the hardware specific work it is good at.

sentences.en: I didn’t actually need the phone to become a normal Linux machine.
sentences.zh: 我实际上并不需要让手机成为一台普通的 Linux 机器。

sentences.en: I needed it to run Linux applications reliably while Android continued doing the hardware specific work it is good at.
sentences.zh: 我需要它可靠地运行 Linux 应用程序，同时 Android 继续执行它擅长的硬件特定工作。

blocks.html_en: termux is the host operating system

sentences.en: termux is the host operating system
sentences.zh: termux 是主机操作系统

blocks.html_en: The second attempt kept stock Android and treated Termux as the host environment.

sentences.en: The second attempt kept stock Android and treated Termux as the host environment.
sentences.zh: 第二次尝试保留了原生 Android 并将 Termux 视为主机环境。

blocks.html_en: Termux gives me OpenSSH, runit, Caddy, Cloudflared, package management, and normal enough Unix tooling. Termux:Boot starts the supervisor and SSH after a reboot. Tailscale gives the phone a stable private address, so from any machine on my tailnet I can just run:

sentences.en: Termux gives me OpenSSH, runit, Caddy, Cloudflared, package management, and normal enough Unix tooling.
sentences.zh: Termux 为我提供了 OpenSSH、runit、Caddy、Cloudflared、包管理和足够普通的 Unix 工具。

sentences.en: Termux:Boot starts the supervisor and SSH after a reboot.
sentences.zh: Termux:Boot 在重新启动后启动 Supervisor 和 SSH。

sentences.en: Tailscale gives the phone a stable private address, so from any machine on my tailnet I can just run:
sentences.zh: Tailscale 为手机提供了一个稳定的私有地址，因此我可以从 tailnet 上的任何机器上运行：

blocks.html_en: Termux is not a virtual machine. Its processes still execute against Android’s Linux kernel, but its Bionic based userspace is different enough from an ordinary Debian installation that existing Linux application images cannot simply be dropped into it. That split ended up being useful, though: Termux could remain the small host control plane while each application brought the Linux filesystem it expected.

sentences.en: Termux is not a virtual machine.
sentences.zh: Termux 不是虚拟机。

sentences.en: Its processes still execute against Android’s Linux kernel, but its Bionic based userspace is different enough from an ordinary Debian installation that existing Linux application images cannot simply be dropped into it.
sentences.zh: 它的进程仍然针对 Android 的 Linux 内核执行，但其基于 Bionic 的用户空间与普通的 Debian 安装有很大不同，现有的 Linux 应用程序映像不能简单地放入其中。

sentences.en: That split ended up being useful, though: Termux could remain the small host control plane while each application brought the Linux filesystem it expected.
sentences.zh: 不过，这种拆分最终是有用的：Termux 可以保留小型主机控制平面，而每个应用程序都带来它所期望的 Linux 文件系统。

blocks.html_en: The actual services are supervised by runit. Android’s battery management is very good at its normal job and very bad for a device pretending to be a server, so I had my Ansible build also apply an Android host profile: it installs a persistent wake lock, disables light and deep idle, exempts Termux, Termux:Boot, and Tailscale from background restrictions, disables the child process limiter, prevents Wi-Fi suspension, and configures Tailscale as the always on VPN.

sentences.en: The actual services are supervised by runit.
sentences.zh: 实际的服务由runit 监管。

sentences.en: Android’s battery management is very good at its normal job and very bad for a device pretending to be a server, so I had my Ansible build also apply an Android host profile: it installs a persistent wake lock, disables light and deep idle, exempts Termux, Termux:Boot, and Tailscale from background restrictions, disables the child process limiter, prevents Wi-Fi suspension, and configures Tailscale as the always on VPN.
sentences.zh: Android 的电池管理在其正常工作中非常出色，但对于伪装成服务器的设备来说非常糟糕，因此我让我的 Ansible 版本也应用了 Android 主机配置文件：它安装了持久唤醒锁，禁用轻度和深度空闲，使 Termux、Termux:Boot 和 Tailscale 免受后台限制，禁用子进程限制器，防止 Wi-Fi 暂停，并将 Tailscale 配置为始终在线的 VPN。

blocks.html_en: The recovery chain matters more than any individual setting. Android boots, always on VPN brings Tailscale back, Termux:Boot starts runit, runit starts every resident service, and health checks verify the local and public paths. The phone can reboot without waiting for me to notice.

sentences.en: The recovery chain matters more than any individual setting.
sentences.zh: 恢复链比任何单独的设置都更重要。

sentences.en: Android boots, always on VPN brings Tailscale back, Termux:Boot starts runit, runit starts every resident service, and health checks verify the local and public paths.
sentences.zh: Android 启动、始终开启 VPN 使 Tailscale 回归，Termux:Boot 启动 runit，runit 启动每个常驻服务，健康检查验证本地和公共路径。

sentences.en: The phone can reboot without waiting for me to notice.
sentences.zh: 手机可以在不等我注意到的情况下重新启动。

blocks.html_en: This isn’t a conventional Linux server. There is no systemd, no normal Docker daemon, and no reason to pretend otherwise. But it is a Linux kernel with a very capable userland sitting on top of it, and that turns out to be enough.

sentences.en: This isn’t a conventional Linux server.
sentences.zh: 这不是传统的 Linux 服务器。

sentences.en: There is no systemd, no normal Docker daemon, and no reason to pretend otherwise.
sentences.zh: 没有 systemd，没有正常的 Docker 守护进程，也没有理由假装不是这样。

sentences.en: But it is a Linux kernel with a very capable userland sitting on top of it, and that turns out to be enough.
sentences.zh: 但它是一个 Linux 内核，上面有一个非常强大的用户空间，事实证明这已经足够了。

blocks.html_en: the second bad idea: proot

sentences.en: the second bad idea: proot
sentences.zh: 第二个坏主意：proot

blocks.html_en: Most of my applications already shipped as Linux ARM64 OCI images. proot-distro made those surprisingly easy to run under Debian without changing the applications themselves.

sentences.en: Most of my applications already shipped as Linux ARM64 OCI images.
sentences.zh: 我的大多数应用程序已作为 Linux ARM64 OCI 映像提供。

sentences.en: proot-distro made those surprisingly easy to run under Debian without changing the applications themselves.
sentences.zh: proot-distro 使这些应用程序能够在 Debian 下轻松运行，而无需更改应用程序本身。

blocks.html_en: PRoot intercepts filesystem and process operations in userspace and makes a regular Termux process believe it lives inside a Debian root filesystem. It isn’t a container boundary. Everything still shares Android’s kernel, network namespace, and Termux UID. But as an application compatibility layer, it is extremely useful because it needs neither root nor a special kernel.

sentences.en: PRoot intercepts filesystem and process operations in userspace and makes a regular Termux process believe it lives inside a Debian root filesystem.
sentences.zh: PRoot 拦截用户空间中的文件系统和进程操作，并使常规 Termux 进程相信它位于 Debian 根文件系统内。

sentences.en: It isn’t a container boundary.
sentences.zh: 它不是容器边界。

sentences.en: Everything still shares Android’s kernel, network namespace, and Termux UID.
sentences.zh: 所有东西仍然共享 Android 的内核、网络命名空间和 Termux UID。

sentences.en: But as an application compatibility layer, it is extremely useful because it needs neither root nor a special kernel.
sentences.zh: 但作为应用程序兼容层，它非常有用，因为它既不需要 root 也不需要特殊的内核。

blocks.html_en: The ordinary web services initially ran fine this way. Each of my applications got a verified root filesystem, a loopback port, and a runit service. Caddy ran directly in Termux and routed hostnames to those ports.

sentences.en: The ordinary web services initially ran fine this way.
sentences.zh: 普通的 Web 服务最初以这种方式运行良好。

sentences.en: Each of my applications got a verified root filesystem, a loopback port, and a runit service.
sentences.zh: 我的每个应用程序都有一个经过验证的根文件系统、一个环回端口和一个 runit 服务。

sentences.en: Caddy ran directly in Termux and routed hostnames to those ports.
sentences.zh: Caddy 直接在 Termux 中运行并将主机名路由到这些端口。

blocks.html_en: The performance/latency sensitive Surf browser workload was the exception. Starting processes, opening libraries, walking paths, reading browser profiles, and shuffling capture data all crossed PRoot’s userspace translation layer. There was CPU available, but Chrome could not reach it efficiently. So I rooted the phone, not to replace Android, but to mount the same Debian filesystem properly and enter it with a real chroot.

sentences.en: The performance/latency sensitive Surf browser workload was the exception.
sentences.zh: 对性能/延迟敏感的 Surf 浏览器工作负载是例外。

sentences.en: Starting processes, opening libraries, walking paths, reading browser profiles, and shuffling capture data all crossed PRoot’s userspace translation layer.
sentences.zh: 启动进程、打开库、行走路径、读取浏览器配置文件以及整理捕获数据都跨越了 PRoot 的用户空间转换层。

sentences.en: There was CPU available, but Chrome could not reach it efficiently.
sentences.zh: 有可用的 CPU，但 Chrome 无法有效地访问它。

sentences.en: So I rooted the phone, not to replace Android, but to mount the same Debian filesystem properly and enter it with a real chroot.
sentences.zh: 所以我root了手机，不是为了更换Android，而是为了正确安装相同的Debian文件系统并使用真正的chroot进入它。

blocks.html_en: Runit still owned the lifecycle from Termux, configuration still came from the same place, and application data still lived in Termux storage. The workload simply reached Android’s kernel through native syscalls instead of PRoot. The improvement was not subtle!

sentences.en: Runit still owned the lifecycle from Termux, configuration still came from the same place, and application data still lived in Termux storage.
sentences.zh: Runit 仍然拥有 Termux 的生命周期，配置仍然来自同一个地方，应用程序数据仍然驻留在 Termux 存储中。

sentences.en: The workload simply reached Android’s kernel through native syscalls instead of PRoot.
sentences.zh: 工作负载只是通过本机系统调用而不是 PRoot 到达 Android 内核。

sentences.en: The improvement was not subtle!
sentences.zh: 改进并不微妙！

blocks.html_en: Once that path was solid, leaving the smaller residents under PRoot stopped making much sense. They now run the same way. My workstation resolves each ARM64 image to an exact digest and exports its filesystem; Ansible verifies and installs it on the phone. A small root helper creates a private mount namespace, binds the required paths, enters the filesystem with chroot, drops privileges, and starts the original image entrypoint.

sentences.en: Once that path was solid, leaving the smaller residents under PRoot stopped making much sense.
sentences.zh: 一旦这条道路变得稳固，将较小的居民留在 PRoot 之下就不再有意义了。

sentences.en: They now run the same way.
sentences.zh: 他们现在以同样的方式运行。

sentences.en: My workstation resolves each ARM64 image to an exact digest and exports its filesystem; Ansible verifies and installs it on the phone.
sentences.zh: 我的工作站将每个 ARM64 映像解析为精确的摘要并导出其文件系统； Ansible 验证并将其安装在手机上。

sentences.en: A small root helper creates a private mount namespace, binds the required paths, enters the filesystem with chroot, drops privileges, and starts the original image entrypoint.
sentences.zh: 一个小的根助手创建一个私有挂载命名空间，绑定所需的路径，使用 chroot 进入文件系统，删除权限，并启动原始图像入口点。

blocks.html_en: Neither Docker nor a compiler needs to exist on the phone. These are still compatibility environments rather than security boundaries: the residents share Android’s kernel and network stack, while the private mount namespaces mainly keep mounts and cleanup predictable.

sentences.en: Neither Docker nor a compiler needs to exist on the phone.
sentences.zh: Docker 和编译器都不需要存在于手机上。

sentences.en: These are still compatibility environments rather than security boundaries: the residents share Android’s kernel and network stack, while the private mount namespaces mainly keep mounts and cleanup predictable.
sentences.zh: 这些仍然是兼容性环境而不是安全边界：居民共享 Android 的内核和网络堆栈，而私有挂载命名空间主要保持挂载和清理的可预测性。

blocks.html_en: I also spent far too long trying to bridge Debian’s graphics stack to the phone’s Mali GPU through VirGL and Android Vulkan. I got hardware compositing checkmarks alongside corrupt pages and worse performance… The boring software rendered path turned out to perform better.

sentences.en: I also spent far too long trying to bridge Debian’s graphics stack to the phone’s Mali GPU through VirGL and Android Vulkan.
sentences.zh: 我还花了很长时间尝试通过 VirGL 和 Android Vulkan 将 Debian 的图形堆栈连接到手机的 Mali GPU。

sentences.en: I got hardware compositing checkmarks alongside corrupt pages and worse performance…
sentences.zh: 我得到了硬件合成复选标记以及损坏的页面和更差的性能......

sentences.en: The boring software rendered path turned out to perform better.
sentences.zh: 无聊的软件渲染路径结果表现得更好。

blocks.html_en: infrastructure! not a pile of shell history

sentences.en: infrastructure!
sentences.zh: 基础设施！

sentences.en: not a pile of shell history
sentences.zh: 不是一堆 shell 历史

blocks.html_en: By this point the phone could run everything, but I didn’t want a pet server assembled from commands I would forget in a week. I moved the entire host into an Ansible managed state: versions, service definitions, routes, power settings, secrets, and health checks all live in one private repository.

sentences.en: By this point the phone could run everything, but I didn’t want a pet server assembled from commands I would forget in a week.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，手机可以运行所有功能，但我不想要一个由我一周后就会忘记的命令组装而成的宠物服务器。

sentences.en: I moved the entire host into an Ansible managed state: versions, service definitions, routes, power settings, secrets, and health checks all live in one private repository.
sentences.zh: 我将整个主机移至 Ansible 托管状态：版本、服务定义、路由、电源设置、机密和运行状况检查都位于一个私有存储库中。

blocks.html_en: The deployment flow is roughly:

sentences.en: The deployment flow is roughly:
sentences.zh: 部署流程大致为：

blocks.html_en: Releases are pinned by digest or checksum and installed into versioned directories behind an atomic current symlink. A failed checksum or health check stops the deployment, rollback means reverting the pin and applying again. Application data lives separately from releases.

sentences.en: Releases are pinned by digest or checksum and installed into versioned directories behind an atomic current symlink.
sentences.zh: 版本由摘要或校验和固定，并安装到原子当前符号链接后面的版本化目录中。

sentences.en: A failed checksum or health check stops the deployment, rollback means reverting the pin and applying again.
sentences.zh: 校验和或运行状况检查失败会停止部署，回滚意味着恢复 pin 并再次应用。

sentences.en: Application data lives separately from releases.
sentences.zh: 应用程序数据与版本分开存在。

blocks.html_en: After the small manual bootstrap: install the three Android apps, root the phone, grant Termux superuser access, and authorize SSH, the same repository owns the rest. From my workstation, bringing the host to the declared state is deliberately simple:

sentences.en: After the small manual bootstrap: install the three Android apps, root the phone, grant Termux superuser access, and authorize SSH, the same repository owns the rest.
sentences.zh: 在小型手动引导程序之后：安装三个 Android 应用程序、root 手机、授予 Termux 超级用户访问权限并授权 SSH，同一存储库拥有其余部分。

sentences.en: From my workstation, bringing the host to the declared state is deliberately simple:
sentences.zh: 从我的工作站，将主机置于声明状态非常简单：

blocks.html_en: Applying it again does not replace unchanged runtime files or restart healthy residents. More importantly, the configuration is useful if this phone dies: another rootable ARM64 phone can be brought toward the same state without reconstructing a shell history.

sentences.en: Applying it again does not replace unchanged runtime files or restart healthy residents.
sentences.zh: 再次应用它不会替换未更改的运行时文件或重新启动健康的居民。

sentences.en: More importantly, the configuration is useful if this phone dies: another rootable ARM64 phone can be brought toward the same state without reconstructing a shell history.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，如果此手机死机，该配置很有用：可以使另一部可 root 的 ARM64 手机进入相同状态，而无需重建 shell 历史记录。

blocks.html_en: Secrets are not stored on the phone’s Git checkout, because there is no Git checkout. Ansible Vault values live encrypted in the infrastructure repository. The vault password is derived by asking my 1Password SSH agent to sign a fixed challenge, so the private key stays in 1Password and the phone never needs access to it. During deployment, Ansible renders only the runtime values each service needs into Termux’s private storage.

sentences.en: Secrets are not stored on the phone’s Git checkout, because there is no Git checkout.
sentences.zh: 秘密不会存储在手机的 Git checkout 上，因为没有 Git checkout。

sentences.en: Ansible Vault values live encrypted in the infrastructure repository.
sentences.zh: Ansible Vault 值在基础设施存储库中实时加密。

sentences.en: The vault password is derived by asking my 1Password SSH agent to sign a fixed challenge, so the private key stays in 1Password and the phone never needs access to it.
sentences.zh: 保管库密码是通过要求我的 1Password SSH 代理签署固定质询而派生的，因此私钥保留在 1Password 中，手机永远不需要访问它。

sentences.en: During deployment, Ansible renders only the runtime values each service needs into Termux’s private storage.
sentences.zh: 在部署期间，Ansible 仅将每个服务所需的运行时值渲染到 Termux 的私有存储中。

blocks.html_en: getting traffic to a phone behind home internet

sentences.en: getting traffic to a phone behind home internet
sentences.zh: 获取家庭互联网后面手机的流量

blocks.html_en: The next problem to tackle was ingress. My home connection does not come with the kind of static server setup a VPS gives you, and I don’t want to expose SSH or a collection of random application ports through the router. I also wanted the phone to remain a phone in one important sense: I should be able to unplug it, take it somewhere else, connect it to the internet, and still have my server.

sentences.en: The next problem to tackle was ingress.
sentences.zh: 下一个要解决的问题是入口。

sentences.en: My home connection does not come with the kind of static server setup a VPS gives you, and I don’t want to expose SSH or a collection of random application ports through the router.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭连接不具备 VPS 提供的那种静态服务器设置，而且我不想通过路由器公开 SSH 或随机应用程序端口的集合。

sentences.en: I also wanted the phone to remain a phone in one important sense: I should be able to unplug it, take it somewhere else, connect it to the internet, and still have my server.
sentences.zh: 我还希望这款手机在一个重要的意义上仍然是一部手机：我应该能够拔掉它，把它带到其他地方，将它连接到互联网，并且仍然拥有我的服务器。

blocks.html_en: The HTTP applications use a Cloudflare Tunnel. Cloudflared makes one outbound connection from the phone, Cloudflare sends each hostname through it, and Caddy routes the request to the correct loopback service.

sentences.en: The HTTP applications use a Cloudflare Tunnel.

content_html_zh:
有一段时间，我的个人基础设施依赖于小型 Hetzner VPS。 它运行一些网络应用程序、一个名为 Surf、Caddy 的远程浏览器以及常见的支持人员。 没有什么特别严重的事情。 它有效，我只是不喜欢为此付费。

我运行的应用程序之一 Surf 使这种妥协难以被忽视。 最便宜的共享机器还可以，直到 Chrome 有真正的工作要做，此时他们感到饥饿。 专用 CPU 机器可以解决这个问题，但每个月的成本足以让个人浏览器感觉像是一项值得怀疑的财务承诺。

购买另一台机器也不是一个有吸引力的逃生口。 DRAM 价格已经变得完全愚蠢，因此组装一个具有足够内存量的新盒子感觉特别不合时宜。 我查看了二手迷你电脑，并短暂考虑过在不使用台式机时将其变成服务器。 然后我想起了我已经拥有的 CMF Phone 1。

八个 ARM 内核、8 GB RAM、128 GB 闪存、Wi-Fi 6、一个 5G 调制解调器和一个内置备用电池，所有这些都连接到 SoC，我觉得它太适合放在抽屉里了。 而且我已经付过钱了。 掸去灰尘并把玩了一段时间后，我决定把手机变成服务器。

如今，它运行 Surf 及其托管 Chrome 实例、我的个人财务跟踪器、屏幕共享服务以及一些较小的网络应用程序。 它们可以在重新启动后存活下来，从 Git 进行部署，并且当手机在网络之间移动时仍然可以访问，因此现在这台机器实际上取代了 VPS。

第一个坏主意：替换android

这个想法最干净的版本似乎是刷新一个普通的 Linux 发行版。 CMF Phone 1 有一个 postmarketOS 设备端口，它会启动，并且设备页面上有足够的绿色框，足以让鲁莽的人乐观起来。 我最终成为了那个人。

我不太关注的是所有被标记为损坏的东西：Wi-Fi、蓝牙、硬件加速以及大多数其他使手机用作小型服务器的东西。 我得到了 postmarketOS 启动画面和黑色显示屏。 那时我既没有服务器也没有电话。

恢复Nothing OS库存变成了它自己的支线任务。 刷机实用程序需要 Windows，因此我在 QEMU 中安装了 Windows，与 USB 直通和 MediaTek 驱动程序进行了斗争，看着刷机工具挂起，然后最终将该过程转移到实际的 Windows 安装中并恢复了出厂映像。

中间有一瞬间，手机软了，只显示黑屏，我真的以为我已经把一个完美的设备变成了镇纸。

它回来了，并吸取了教训：Android 已经为该硬件的每个部分提供了可用的驱动程序。 Wi-Fi、电源管理、电池、GPU、调制解调器以及每一个奇怪的供应商细节都已经可以工作了。 为了追求更传统的用户空间而抛弃所有这些是错误的做法。

我实际上并不需要让手机成为一台普通的 Linux 机器。 我需要它可靠地运行 Linux 应用程序，同时 Android 继续执行它擅长的硬件特定工作。

termux 是主机操作系统

第二次尝试保留了原生 Android 并将 Termux 视为主机环境。

Termux 为我提供了 OpenSSH、runit、Caddy、Cloudflared、包管理和足够普通的 Unix 工具。 Termux:Boot 在重新启动后启动 Supervisor 和 SSH。 Tailscale 为手机提供了一个稳定的私有地址，因此我可以从 tailnet 上的任何机器上运行：

ssh cmf

Termux 不是虚拟机。 它的进程仍然针对 Android 的 Linux 内核执行，但其基于 Bionic 的用户空间与普通的 Debian 安装有很大不同，现有的 Linux 应用程序映像不能简单地放入其中。 不过，这种拆分最终是有用的：Termux 可以保留小型主机控制平面，而每个应用程序都带来它所期望的 Linux 文件系统。

实际的服务由runit 监管。 Android 的电池管理在其正常工作中非常出色，但对于伪装成服务器的设备来说非常糟糕，因此我让我的 Ansible 版本也应用了 Android 主机配置文件：它安装了持久唤醒锁，禁用轻度和深度空闲，使 Termux、Termux:Boot 和 Tailscale 免受后台限制，禁用子进程限制器，防止 Wi-Fi 暂停，并将 Tailscale 配置为始终在线的 VPN。

恢复链比任何单独的设置都更重要。 Android 启动、始终开启 VPN 使 Tailscale 回归，Termux:Boot 启动 runit，runit 启动每个常驻服务，健康检查验证本地和公共路径。 手机可以在不等我注意到的情况下重新启动。

Android boot
  -> Tailscale always-on VPN
  -> Termux:Boot
  -> runit
  -> resident services
  -> local and public health checks

这不是传统的 Linux 服务器。 没有 systemd，没有正常的 Docker 守护进程，也没有理由假装不是这样。 但它是一个 Linux 内核，上面有一个非常强大的用户空间，事实证明这已经足够了。

第二个坏主意：proot

我的大多数应用程序已作为 Linux ARM64 OCI 映像提供。 proot-distro 使这些应用程序能够在 Debian 下轻松运行，而无需更改应用程序本身。

PRoot 拦截用户空间中的文件系统和进程操作，并使常规 Termux 进程相信它位于 Debian 根文件系统内。 它不是容器边界。 所有东西仍然共享 Android 的内核、网络命名空间和 Termux UID。 但作为应用程序兼容层，它非常有用，因为它既不需要 root 也不需要特殊的内核。

普通的 Web 服务最初以这种方式运行良好。 我的每个应用程序都有一个经过验证的根文件系统、一个环回端口和一个 runit 服务。 Caddy 直接在 Termux 中运行并将主机名路由到这些端口。

对性能/延迟敏感的 Surf 浏览器工作负载是例外。 启动进程、打开库、行走路径、读取浏览器配置文件以及整理捕获数据都跨越了 PRoot 的用户空间转换层。 有可用的 CPU，但 Chrome 无法有效地访问它。 所以我root了手机，不是为了更换Android，而是为了正确安装相同的Debian文件系统并使用真正的chroot进入它。

Runit 仍然拥有 Termux 的生命周期，配置仍然来自同一个地方，应用程序数据仍然驻留在 Termux 存储中。 工作负载只是通过本机系统调用而不是 PRoot 到达 Android 内核。 改进并不微妙！

一旦这条道路变得稳固，将较小的居民留在 PRoot 之下就不再有意义了。 他们现在以同样的方式运行。 我的工作站将每个 ARM64 映像解析为精确的摘要并导出其文件系统； Ansible 验证并将其安装在手机上。 一个小的根助手创建一个私有挂载命名空间，绑定所需的路径，使用 chroot 进入文件系统，删除权限，并启动原始图像入口点。

Docker 和编译器都不需要存在于手机上。 这些仍然是兼容性环境而不是安全边界：居民共享 Android 的内核和网络堆栈，而私有挂载命名空间主要保持挂载和清理的可预测性。

我还花了很长时间尝试通过 VirGL 和 Android Vulkan 将 Debian 的图形堆栈连接到手机的 Mali GPU。 我得到了硬件合成复选标记以及损坏的页面和更差的性能...... 无聊的软件渲染路径结果表现得更好。

基础设施！ 不是一堆 shell 历史

到目前为止，手机可以运行所有功能，但我不想要一个由我一周后就会忘记的命令组装而成的宠物服务器。 我将整个主机移至 Ansible 托管状态：版本、服务定义、路由、电源设置、机密和运行状况检查都位于一个私有存储库中。

部署流程大致为：

release or OCI image
  -> checksum/digest pinned in Git
  -> Ansible over SSH
  -> versioned files on the phone
  -> atomic current symlink
  -> runit service
  -> local health check
  -> public edge check

版本由摘要或校验和固定，并安装到原子当前符号链接后面的版本化目录中。 校验和或运行状况检查失败会停止部署，回滚意味着恢复 pin 并再次应用。 应用程序数据与版本分开存在。

在小型手动引导程序之后：安装三个 Android 应用程序、root 手机、授予 Termux 超级用户访问权限并授权 SSH，同一存储库拥有其余部分。 从我的工作站，将主机置于声明状态非常简单：

make phone
make phone-status
make phone-edge-check

再次应用它不会替换未更改的运行时文件或重新启动健康的居民。 更重要的是，如果此手机死机，该配置很有用：可以使另一部可 root 的 ARM64 手机进入相同状态，而无需重建 shell 历史记录。

秘密不会存储在手机的 Git checkout 上，因为没有 Git checkout。 Ansible Vault 值在基础设施存储库中实时加密。 保管库密码是通过要求我的 1Password SSH 代理签署固定质询而派生的，因此私钥保留在 1Password 中，手机永远不需要访问它。 在部署期间，Ansible 仅将每个服务所需的运行时值渲染到 Termux 的私有存储中。

获取家庭互联网后面手机的流量

下一个要解决的问题是入口。 我的家庭连接不具备 VPS 提供的那种静态服务器设置，而且我不想通过路由器公开 SSH 或随机应用程序端口的集合。 我还希望这款手机在一个重要的意义上仍然是一部手机：我应该能够拔掉它，把它带到其他地方，将它连接到互联网，并且仍然拥有我的服务器。

HTTP 应用程序使用 Cloudflare 隧道。 Cloudflared 从电话建立一个出站连接，Cloudflare 通过它发送每个主机名，Caddy 将请求路由到正确的环回服务。

Internet
  -> Cloudflare Tunnel
  -> Caddy on 127.0.0.1
  -> application on 127.0.0.1

这些服务没有入站路由器规则。 Cloudflared 仅需要出站连接，因此如果我将手机移至另一个网络，隧道将重新连接，主机名也会随之变化。 Tailscale 对管理也做了同样的事情。 手机的电池可以桥接移动，而公共服务并不关心它们下面恰好有哪个 Wi-Fi。

不过，Surf 远程浏览器后端需要不同的路径。 它的直接连接对延迟敏感，会终止自己的 TLS，并且连接到它的旧 iPad 会固定服务器身份。 在家里，Cloudflare DDNS 仅保留指向当前公共地址的 DNS 记录，并且路由器将一个端口转发到 Surf。 在 LAN 上，iPad 直接连接到手机。

那仍然是漫游。 普通的 Cloudflare Tunnel 在 Cloudflare 处终止 TLS，这正是 Surf 的固定连接所不希望看到的。 解决方案是将完整的 Surf TLS 流包装在普通的 WebSocket 中。 Cloudflare 会看到并转发 WebSocket，但实际经过身份验证的 Surf 连接在其内部仍保持端到端加密。

这显然增加了延迟，在外面我通常会看到大约另一个网络往返，当我第一次测试时，iPad 连接大约是 60 毫秒。 但它可以在 2012 年的操作系统上通过隧道运行，只需要出站连接，无需在 iPad 上安装 Tailscale。

就在那时，手机设置变得有点荒谬。 我把它留在家里，然后去了办公室，通过 Tailscale 从我的 MacBook 通过 SSH 连接到我的工作站和手机，并通过手机托管的 Surf 实例使用原来的 iPad。 VPS 不再是，它给人一种解放的感觉。

实际运行的是什么

该机器有两层。 Android 和 Termux 拥有硬件、网络、入口和监管。 Linux 居民可以获得他们期望的文件系统，并且不会妨碍主机。

layer责任件
Android / Termux 主机硬件、网络、入口、监控runit、Tailscale、Caddy、Cloudflared、DDNS、操作仪表板
已root的Linux居民应用程序兼容性和工作负载Surf 和 Chrome、财务、屏幕共享以及其他一些应用程序

Surf 是要求较高的工作负载，它为旧 iPhone 和 iPad 带来了现代 Chromium 浏览器。 该手机运行桌面 Chrome（Chrome 最近发布的 arm64 版本）和 Debian 运行时内的 Surf 后端，iPad mini 接收 H.264 视频和音频，同时发送触摸、键盘、选项卡和导航命令。 Surf 是我首先如此关心系统调用开销和延迟的原因。

除此之外，手机上还装有我的个人财务跟踪器。 它记录经常性收入和支出、一次性交易、每月支出限额，并逐日预测我的余额。 与可替换的应用程序工件不同，它的 SQLite 数据库包含我关心的状态，因此它具有自动的设备外备份和经过测试的恢复路径。

这些名称都没有被纳入某种宏伟的“电话服务器框架”中。 新居民是另一个不可变的工件，一个 runit 定义，一个显式数据契约，一个健康检查，以及一个可选的 Caddy 路由。

最新增加的是可观察性。 我仍然可以通过 SSH 登录、检查 runit、尾部日志、检查公共路由以及直接查询 Android，但我不再需要仅仅为了一目了然地了解机器的运行情况而这样做：一个本机服务收集所有八个内核的 CPU 使用情况、内存、存储、正常运行时间、电池、热量、本地和公共可达性以及每个发现的 runit 驻留。 它保留有限的历史记录，并在 https://dash.cmf 上提供嵌入式 Vue 接口，只能通过 LAN 或 tailnet 访问。

日志视图在运行时发现相同的服务目录，因此添加另一个驻留者不需要向 UI 告知其名称。 这比仅仅通过 SSH 登录来记住哪个东西发出噪音要好得多。

你应该这样做吗？

如果您已经拥有一部相当现代、可 root 的 ARM64 手机但未使用，那么这并不像听起来那么荒谬。 您可以获得安静的硬件、低功耗、闪存、Wi-Fi、用于恢复的内置显示器以及像微型 UPS 一样的电池。 原生 Android 已经支持该硬件，而 Termux 和 root 的 chroot 足以运行数量惊人的普通 Linux 软件。

如果没有自动设备外备份，我不会将不可替代的数据放在其中，并且我不会将 chroot 视为敌对工作负载隔离。 Root 扩展了信任边界，Android 仍然是一个不寻常的服务器主机，软件渲染的桌面 Chrome 不会击败带有 GPU 的专用工作站。

但对于少数个人服务来说，尤其是当替代方案是无限期支付速度缓慢或昂贵得令人恼火的 VPS 时，这是一个真正有用的选择，而不仅仅是一个噱头。

电话仍然是一个奇怪的服务器。 它共享一个内核，Android偶尔需要提醒不要“优化”它，未来的Android更新总能创造新的惊喜。

但它很安静，有电池支持，速度足够快，可以从任何地方访问，可以从 Git 复制，而且已经放在我家里了。 我开始尝试在 VPS 上省钱。 我最终得到了一部运行我的个人基础设施的手机，不知何故，这更令人满意。 :)
